'''Auke Jan Ijspeert''' (born 1971 in [[Geneva]]) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]]-[[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Robotics|roboticist]] and [[neuroscientist]]. He is a professor of  biorobotics in the Institute of Bioengineering at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]], École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, and the head of the Biorobotics Laboratory at the School of Engineering.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Biorobotics Laboratory (BioRob)|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=21 professors appointed at ETH Zurich and EPFL {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/21-professorinnen-und-professoren-den-beiden-eth-ernannt|access-date=2020-12-03|website=www.ethrat.ch}}</ref>

== Career ==

He has studied [[physics]] at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] and 
a degree of an "Ingénieur physicien" (equivalent to [[Master's degree]]) in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Getting into Robotics: Auke Ijspeert – NCCR Robotics|url=https://nccr-robotics.ch/kids-teachers-parents/how-to-be-a-roboticist/how-our-professors-got-into-robotics/auke-ijspeert/|access-date=2020-12-03|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Ijspeert|first=Auke|title=Auke Ijspeert {{!}} Speaker {{!}} TED|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/auke_ijspeert|access-date=2020-12-03|website=www.ted.com|language=en}}</ref> He joined John Hallam and [[David Willshaw]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]] as a doctoral student, and in 1999 graduated with a PhD in artificial intelligence on the "Design of artificial neural oscillatory circuits for the control of lamprey- and salamander-like locomotion using evolutionary algorithms".<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Design of artificial neural oscillatory circuits for the control of lamprey- and salamander-like locomotion using evolutionary algorithms|url=https://hdl.handle.net/1842/34726|publisher=University of Edinburgh|date=1999|degree=Ph.D.|first=Auke Jan|last=Ijspeert|hdl=1842/34726}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ijspeert|first1=Auke Jan|last2=Hallam|first2=John|last3=Willshaw|first3=David|date=2016-07-25|title=Evolving Swimming Controllers for a Simulated Lamprey with Inspiration from Neurobiology|url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/105971239900700202|journal=Adaptive Behavior|volume=7|issue=2|pages=151–172|language=en|doi=10.1177/105971239900700202|s2cid=16472569|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] with [[Michael A. Arbib]] and [[Stefan Schaal]] at [[University of Southern California]] (USC),<ref>{{Citation|chapter=Visual tracking in simulated salamander locomotion|date=2000|chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/3120.003.0011|title=From Animals to Animats 6|publisher=The MIT Press|doi=10.7551/mitpress/3120.003.0011|isbn=978-0-262-31607-1|access-date=2020-12-03 |last1=Ijspeert |first1=Auke Jan |last2=Arbib |first2=Michael |pages=88–97 |chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ijspeert|first1=Auke Jan|last2=Arbib|first2=Michael A.|editor-first1=Gerard T. |editor-first2=Paul S. |editor-last1=McKee |editor-last2=Schenker |date=2000-10-16|title=Locomotion and visually guided behavior in salamander: a neuromechanical study|url=https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/conference-proceedings-of-spie/4196/0000/Locomotion-and-visually-guided-behavior-in-salamander--a-neuromechanical/10.1117/12.403749.short|journal=Sensor Fusion and Decentralized Control in Robotic Systems III|publisher=International Society for Optics and Photonics|volume=4196|pages=62–71|doi=10.1117/12.403749|bibcode=2000SPIE.4196...62I|s2cid=85038783|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and then at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] with [[Jean-Daniel Nicoud]] and with [[Luca Maria Gambardella]] ([[Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research]] - IDSIA).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ijspeert|first1=Auke Jan|last2=Martinoli|first2=Alcherio|last3=Billard|first3=Aude|last4=Gambardella|first4=Luca Maria|date=2001-09-01|title=Collaboration Through the Exploitation of Local Interactions in Autonomous Collective Robotics: The Stick Pulling Experiment|url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1011227210047|journal=Autonomous Robots|language=en|volume=11|issue=2|pages=149–171|doi=10.1023/A:1011227210047|s2cid=11370718|issn=1573-7527|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2001, he became a research assistant professor at the Department of Computer Science of the [[University of Southern California]], and an external collaborator at [[Kansai Science City|ATR]] (Advanced Telecommunications Research institute) in [[Japan]].<ref name="dx.doi.org">{{Cite journal|last1=Ijspeert|first1=Auke Jan|last2=Nakanishi|first2=Jun|last3=Hoffmann|first3=Heiko|last4=Pastor|first4=Peter|last5=Schaal|first5=Stefan|date=February 2013|title=Dynamical Movement Primitives: Learning Attractor Models for Motor Behaviors|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1162/neco_a_00393|journal=Neural Computation|volume=25|issue=2|pages=328–373|doi=10.1162/neco_a_00393|pmid=23148415|bibcode=2013NeCom..25..328I |s2cid=2431443|issn=0899-7667|via=|hdl=20.500.11820/3a347438-6b51-4f11-ba7a-5465173736f8|hdl-access=free}}</ref> From 2003 to 2017, he was an adjunct faculty Department of Computer Science of the [[University of Southern California]]. In 2002, he received [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] assistant professorship at the School of Computer and Communication Sciences of [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]. In 2009, he was named associate professor at EPFL's School of Engineering, and in 2016 he was promoted as full professor.<ref name=":1" /> He leads the Biorobotics Laboratory at the School of Engineering.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
The Ijspeert group's [[Transdisciplinarity|transdisciplinary research]] is situated at the intersection of [[robotics]], [[computational neuroscience]], [[nonlinear dynamical systems]], and [[Machine learning|applied machine learning]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/|access-date=2020-12-03|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> Employing numerical simulations and [[robot]]s, they aim at a better understanding of [[animal locomotion]] and movement control, and by taking inspiration in nature, they design new types of robots and locomotion controllers.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ijspeert|first1=A. J.|last2=Crespi|first2=A.|last3=Ryczko|first3=D.|last4=Cabelguen|first4=J.-M.|date=2007-03-09|title=From Swimming to Walking with a Salamander Robot Driven by a Spinal Cord Model|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.1138353|journal=Science|volume=315|issue=5817|pages=1416–1420|doi=10.1126/science.1138353|pmid=17347441|bibcode=2007Sci...315.1416I|s2cid=3193002|issn=0036-8075}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ijspeert|first=A. J.|date=2014-10-09|title=Biorobotics: Using robots to emulate and investigate agile locomotion|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1126/science.1254486|journal=Science|volume=346|issue=6206|pages=196–203|doi=10.1126/science.1254486|pmid=25301621|bibcode=2014Sci...346..196I|s2cid=42734749|issn=0036-8075}}</ref> Their research was featured in public presentations at [[TED (conference)|TED Global]] and [[World.minds]] conferences.<ref>{{Citation|last=Ijspeert|first=Auke|title=A robot that runs and swims like a salamander|date=28 January 2016 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/auke_ijspeert_a_robot_that_runs_and_swims_like_a_salamander|language=en|access-date=2020-12-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=23 May 2018|title=Auke Ijspeert: Animal Locomotion – Learning from Robots (WORLD.MINDS MOBILITY 2018)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YbD5WmosseE|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611115641/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YbD5WmosseE |archive-date=2020-06-11 |access-date=|website=Youtube}}</ref>

Their research is focused on computational aspects of locomotion control, [[sensory-motor coupling|sensorimotor]] coordination, and learning in animals and in robots. Furthermore, their research focuses also on [[rehabilitation robotics]], such as [[exoskeleton]]s, and in locomotion restoration. Their interests extent to research projects in areas such as neuromechanical simulations of locomotion and movement control;<ref name="dx.doi.org"/> systems of coupled nonlinear oscillators for locomotion control;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dzeladini|first1=Florin|last2=van den Kieboom|first2=Jesse|last3=Ijspeert|first3=Auke|date=2014-06-26|title=The contribution of a central pattern generator in a reflex-based neuromuscular model|url= |journal=Frontiers in Human Neuroscience|volume=8|page=371|doi=10.3389/fnhum.2014.00371|pmid=25018712|pmc=4071613|issn=1662-5161|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Minassian|first1=Karen|last2=Hofstoetter|first2=Ursula S.|last3=Dzeladini|first3=Florin|last4=Guertin|first4=Pierre A.|last5=Ijspeert|first5=Auke|date=2017-03-28|title=The Human Central Pattern Generator for Locomotion: Does It Exist and Contribute to Walking?|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1177/1073858417699790|journal=The Neuroscientist|volume=23|issue=6|pages=649–663|doi=10.1177/1073858417699790|pmid=28351197|s2cid=33273662|issn=1073-8584|url-access=subscription}}</ref> design and control of [[Amphibian|amphibious]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Amphibious Robotics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/amphibious/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> legged,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Quadruped Robotics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/quadruped/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> and reconfigurable robots;<ref>{{Cite web|title=Modular Robotics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/modular/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> and, control of [[humanoid robot]]s,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Humanoid Robotics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/research/humanoid/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> and of [[exoskeleton]]s.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Noot|first1=N. Van der|last2=Colasanto|first2=L.|last3=Barrea|first3=A.|last4=Kieboom|first4=J. van den|last5=Ronsse|first5=R.|last6=Ijspeert|first6=A. J.|title=2015 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) |chapter=Experimental validation of a bio-inspired controller for dynamic walking with a humanoid robot |date=September 2015|chapter-url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/7353403|volume=|pages=393–400|doi=10.1109/IROS.2015.7353403|isbn=978-1-4799-9994-1|s2cid=2744219|url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/handle/20.500.14299/122622 |via=}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last1=Wu|first1=Amy R.|chapter=A Versatile Neuromuscular Exoskeleton Controller for Gait Assistance: A Preliminary Study on Spinal Cord Injury Patients|date=2017|chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-46532-6_27|title=Wearable Robotics: Challenges and Trends|volume=16|pages=163–167|editor-last=González-Vargas|editor-first=José|place=Cham|publisher=Springer International Publishing|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-46532-6_27|isbn=978-3-319-46531-9|access-date=2020-12-07|last2=Dzeladini|first2=Florin|last3=Brug|first3=Tycho J. == Distinctions ==
Ijspeert is an [[IEEE Fellow]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 IEEE RAS Fellow Class Announced - IEEE Robotics and Automation Society|url=https://www.ieee-ras.org/about-ras/latest-news/17-news-ras-homepage-latest-news/1536-2020-ieee-ras-fellow-class-announced|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.ieee-ras.org|language=en-gb}}</ref> He is a member of the board of reviewing editors of [[Science (journal)|Science Magazine]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-01-31|title=Editors and Advisory Boards|url=https://www.sciencemag.org/about/editors-and-editorial-boards|access-date=2020-12-07|website=Science {{!}} AAAS|language=en}}</ref> and an associate editor of Soft Robotics,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Soft Robotics {{!}} Mary Ann Liebert, Inc., publishers|url=https://home.liebertpub.com/publications/soft-robotics/616/editorial-board|access-date=2020-12-07|website=home.liebertpub.com}}</ref> IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and [[Bionics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1109/TMRB.2020.3033235|doi-access=free |year=2020|volume=2|issue=4|pages=C2 |title= IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics}}</ref> and for the [[International Journal of Humanoid Robotics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=IJHR Editorial Board|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijhr/editorial-board|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.worldscientific.com}}</ref> He has been an associate editor for the [[IEEE Transactions]] on Robotics (2009-2013) and a guest editor for the Proceedings of IEEE, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, Autonomous Robots, IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine, and Biological Cybernetics.

He is a recipient of the Young Professorship Award (2002), the Young Researcher Scholarship (1999), and the Young Researcher Scholarship (1995) all awarded from the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] .<ref>{{Cite web|title=Auke Jan Ijspeert|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/people/ijspeert/|access-date=2020-12-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> He also received the Marie Curie Scholarship from the [[European Commission]] (1997).<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Curriculum Vitae Auke Jan Ijspeert|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/CV_Ijspeert_SHORT_Dec_2016.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924032508/https://www.epfl.ch/labs/biorob/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/CV_Ijspeert_SHORT_Dec_2016.pdf |archive-date=2021-09-24 |access-date=|website=EPFL}}</ref>

== Public involvements ==
Ijspeert is also involved in his local church, the parish of [[Écublens, Vaud|Ecublens]]-[[Saint-Sulpice, Vaud|St-Sulpice]] that is part of the [[Evangelical Reformed Church of the Canton of Vaud]], and he is member of its parish council since 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-05-19|title=Nouveau Conseil paroissial|url=https://ecublenssaintsulpice.eerv.ch/nouveau-conseil-paroissial/|access-date=2021-06-16|website=Paroisse d'Ecublens - Saint-Sulpice|language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Accueil|url=https://ecublenssaintsulpice.eerv.ch/|access-date=2021-06-16|website=Paroisse d'Ecublens - Saint-Sulpice|language=fr-FR}}</ref>
